title: Blog Content Package v0.1
description: One draft blog post, ready for a human to publish. The lane's terminal artifact: the runtime never publishes, so this record is where automation stops and the operator takes over. It carries the draft AND the evidence the topic was chosen on, because a package whose numbers cannot be traced is indistinguishable from a guess. `published_url` is written back by the operator after publishing — without it the lane cannot track ranking and the feedback loop is open.

target_keyword.description: The one keyword this post is written to rank for. Exactly one, deliberately: a draft targeting three keywords ranks for none, and the ranking tracker needs a single subject.

keyword_evidence.description: Why this keyword. Required even when empty-because-degraded, so a package built without live research says so rather than looking researched.

degraded.description: True when the research backend failed and this package carries no measured demand. A consumer must not present a degraded package as evidence-backed.

low_volume.description: The source returned the '< 10' sentinel rather than a number, so these counts are an estimate.

total_competing_posts.description: Naver's own count of blog documents already matching the target keyword.

trend_points.description: Relative search interest, normalised to the peak of the requested window. Comparable within this array only — never across packages.

title_candidates.description: Alternatives for the operator to choose from, not a ranking. Each should carry the target keyword near the front.

body_paste.description: The body exactly as it should be pasted into the Naver SmartEditor: plain text, paragraphs separated by newlines, NO markdown. SmartEditor has no HTML mode and does not interpret markdown, so '##' and '**' would land in the published post as literal characters. All formatting intent lives in `body_blocks` instead.

body_blocks.description: What to do to the pasted text in the editor, addressed by paragraph index. The split between this and `body_paste` is the whole point of the two-file output.

tags.description: Naver caps a post at 30 tags.

image_shots.description: Screens for the operator to capture — not generated images. Posts about using an AI tool need the tool's actual screen; a generated illustration reduces trust and, repeated across posts, becomes a tell.

fact_checks.description: Statements the operator must verify before publishing — prices, free-tier limits, feature availability. These change without notice, and a wrong one in a small-business how-to costs the reader money.

publish_state.description: `draft` until the operator publishes and returns the URL. The runtime never sets this to `published` on its own — it has no way to observe a publish it did not perform.

then.description: A package cannot claim to be published without the URL — that URL is the only input the ranking tracker has, and a `published` state without one silently ends the feedback loop.
